podcast.title: Signing of Hank Williams (1947)
podcast.body: MGM Records signed Hank Williams in 1947, a pivotal moment that led to the release of "Movito Nover" and his subsequent appearance on the Louisiana Hayride radio program. "su carrera daría un cambio en 1947, cuando firmó por NGM Records."

podcast.title: Blackboard Jungle Release (1955)
podcast.body: MGM released the film *Blackboard Jungle* in 1955. This movie was significant for featuring Bill Haley and the Comets' "Rock Around the Clock" in its opening titles, marking the first time a rock and roll song was used in a Hollywood feature film. "In 1955, MGM released Blackboard Jungle, a film about an interracial intercity school."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Million-Dollar Advance (1965)
podcast.body: MGM Records offered Roy Orbison a million-dollar advance to sign with them, a deal brokered by his manager Wesley Rose who was in conflict with Monument's Fred Foster. However, immediately after Orbison signed with MGM, his string of hit records dried up. "Wesley Rose and Fred Foster had never got on, and Rose decided that he was going to move Orbison over to MGM Records, who gave him her advance of a million dollars, but immediately the hits dried up."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Genie C. Riley's Move for Autonomy
podcast.body: Genie C. Riley moved to MGM Records after breaking her contract with Shelby Singleton's Plantation label, seeking to gain more control over her career and personal image. "Eventually, Riley broke her contract with Singleton and went to MGM to try to assert some control over her own career and her life."

podcast.title: National Distribution for C.W. McCall
podcast.body: MGM Records, a prominent major label, recognized the regional success of C. W. McCall's debut single, "Old Home Filler Up and Keep a Truck in the Cafe." Subsequently, MGM signed the fictional artist to provide national distribution, a move that ultimately led to the chart-topping hit "Convoy." "The major label MGM records took notice and signed C. W. McCall to provide national distribution."
